newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends mostly lower on bear spreading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends mostly lower on bear spreading.

text.p: CBOT rice futures, after opening higher on USDA weekly export data, closed lower on bear spreading ahead of first notice day, traders said.
"We opened up strong on export shipments," a floor source said. "Shipments were the highest of the year."
USDA on Thursday put rice exports at 108,300 tonnes, a marketing year high and more than three times the four week average. Export sales of 19,000 tonnes were 52 percent below the four-week average.
Spread trade continued to be the dominant feature as the May contract neared first notice day on Wednesday.
"The spread traded around even to two cents (premium July)," a trader said.
Rice ended steady to five cents per cwt lower with May down five at $11.53.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 500 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 632 lots.
